lectures.title: Managing Layer 1: Controlling Physical Devices with Software

cues.en: Let's now have a look at how we can influence Layer one, meaning that we can enable or disable a device.
So the layer one was more like the physical connection.
And at least from a software side, we can't unplug a cable.
But the only thing we can do to influence this layer is that we can just disable a device through software.
This will then just tell the device, Hey, turn off.
And then of course, layer one won't work because the device has been told by software, Hey, it should
not be active.
And then usually the network card goes into a deep sleep or the network interface is no longer active.
So the way to go is if we want to disable a device through software, is that you first need to get
the name of our device IP addr show, and after that we can enable or disable the device IP link set.
Then the device.
And then we need to provide the name and then we can either enable that device or we can disable that
device.
So as an example, IP link set and then the device name down, that would then, for example, shut
down that device.
Be careful here.
This will just disable the network device.
It usually should not ask you for that.
It will just do it.
So if you're, for example, using a remote machine and you're using this device to connect to that
remote machine, it will just drop our connection and it's not going to work.
So just be aware of that.
So here I am on my ubuntu and we can see here internet is working.
I can just refresh the page.

like this, but they might depend on the order in which they were initialized.

reliable.
